Display compositing? What is it and which one should you use?

This contains some info that linux gamers could benefit from and clears up some questions I had.

So, in many games, i would turn on vsync but still see tearing and I didn't know why. I could also turn on the option in the Nvidia X Server Settings, but again, I'd still get tearing in some games.

I just added the { ForceFullCompositionPipeline = On } modifier and I'm about to reboot. I'm curious if it will get rid of tearing in normal application windows, not just games.

As far as I can tell in some distros certian config settings are overwriting whatever Nvidia X Server Settings creates. I have an issue with a cheap TV I bought where the red coloring bleeds out(like if there's a fire on screen it will bleed into faces etc.) The only way to fix it is to adjust Nvidia settings with only the red setting. But something is overwriting that at startup so I have to adjust it every time. The beauty of an xorg.conf file is that it overwrites everything.

It'll work for most games, but some will still have some level of tearing, such as Divinity Original Sin.

Tearing in general will be gone though with that setting. I use it with no additional compositor in XFCE and haven't had any problems yet.

I've also setup a shortcut to re-apply the setting if a full screen application overrides it.
